text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The head of parliament's foreign affairs committee, Indulis Berzinsh, says the licence agreement between Latvia and oil companies Amoco and OPAB may be retified at the second reading on either October 24 or 31. The agreement's first reading is scheduled for today.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele opened the international conference-exhibition Banking and Finance in the Baltics'96.

- Former Prime Minister Maris Gailis held a news conference to announce that he has become a subject of slanderous attacks by certain groups because of his running for the post of chief manager in the port of Riga. To head off further attacks, Gailis announced that in the morning of the day of the collapse of Banka Baltija he spent 100 lats with his credit card while abroad but the bank stopped its operations in the afternoon.

- OSCE commissioner Max van der Stoel announced at a press conference that there is no systematic violation of human rights in Latvia. He also expressed hope that the number of those claiming Latvia's citizenship, mostly Russian speakers, will increase from its current very low levels.

- The parliamentary party and the board of the Democratic Party Saimnieks called for introducing significant changes in next year's budget draft. They say that otherwise the faction may reject the budget or even quit the government.
- Postage tariffs are likely to be increased in a few months.
- U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry sent letters to his Baltic counterparts in which he announces that he sees Latvia, Estonia and Lithuania as potential members of the NATO.
- Today the parliament will discuss the candidatures of four judges, proposed for the Constitutional Court.

- Last night at 3:00 A.M. two gangsters attacked a currency exchange office in the centre of Riga. Having killed the guard and wounded the cashier and seller, they took away 25,000 German marks and $5,000.
